# restate_cloud_api_key (Resource)

An environment-scoped Restate Cloud API key.

The bearer secret is returned by the create call and never again: it cannot be read back, and it cannot be recovered by an import. It is stored in Terraform state, marked sensitive. **Terraform state therefore contains a live credential** -- use an encrypted, access-controlled state backend.

The Cloud Management API has no update operation for keys, so changing any attribute replaces the key. Replacement mints a new secret and revokes the old one, which breaks anything still authenticating with it. Use `create_before_destroy` if a consumer needs an overlap.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The bearer secret is returned when a key is created and never again, so Terraform state holds the
# only copy. Use an encrypted, access-controlled backend.

# The credential a later Terraform stage configures its Admin API provider with. AdminAccess can
# manage configuration but cannot invoke services, which is the right scope for a Terraform run.
resource "restate_cloud_api_key" "terraform" {
  environment_id = restate_cloud_environment.production.id
  role_id        = "rst:role::AdminAccess"
  description    = "terraform stage 2"
}

# An ingress-only key for application traffic, which should not be able to change configuration.
resource "restate_cloud_api_key" "ingress" {
  environment_id = restate_cloud_environment.production.id
  role_id        = "rst:role::IngressAccess"
  description    = "order service ingress"

  # Any change to a key replaces it, revoking the old secret. Mint the replacement first so a
  # running consumer is never left without a valid credential.
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

output "ingress_api_key" {
  value     = restate_cloud_api_key.ingress.api_key
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment the key grants access to. Changing it replaces the key: a key is minted for one environment and cannot be moved.
- `role_id` (String) Role the key grants: one of `rst:role::FullAccess`, `rst:role::IngressAccess`, `rst:role::AdminAccess`, `rst:role::CompleteAwakeableAccess`, `rst:role::TunnelAccess`.

`rst:role::ManagementApiAccess` is an account-scoped role and is rejected here: it is the provider's own credential, is bootstrapped outside Terraform, and granting it to an environment key would be a privilege escalation.

Changing the role replaces the key, because the API has no update operation.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description, useful for identifying a key in the Restate Cloud console. Changing it replaces the key: the API has no update operation, so there is no way to edit a description in place. Omit it instead of setting an empty string.

### Read-Only

- `account_id` (String) Account the key belongs to. It is the first part of the import ID.
- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) The bearer secret. Available only from the create response.

It is null for an imported key, because the API cannot return it. A configuration that needs the secret must either supply it separately or replace the key with `terraform taint`/`-replace`.
- `id` (String) Key ID assigned by Restate Cloud. A key ID is unique within an environment, not globally.
- `state` (String) Key lifecycle state: `ACTIVE` or `DELETED`. A key reported as `DELETED` is removed from state.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A key ID is only unique within an environment, so the import ID carries account, environment, and
# key. The bearer secret CANNOT be recovered by an import -- Restate Cloud returns it only when the
# key is created. After importing, `api_key` is null; the provider warns about this.
terraform import restate_cloud_api_key.terraform acc_1a2b3c/env_1a2b3c/key_1a2b3c
```
